title: 2025 AMC 10B Problem 10
statement: Let \(f(n) = n^3 - 5n^2 + 2n + 8,\) and let \(g(n) = n^3 - 6n^2 + 5n + 12.\) What is the sum of all integer values of \(n\) for which \(\dfrac{f(n)}{g(n)}\) is also an integer?

solutions.text: Factor both cubics: \(f(n) = (n + 1)(n - 2)(n - 4)\) and \(g(n) = (n + 1)(n - 3)(n - 4).\) Away from \(n \in \{-1, 3, 4\},\) where \(g\) vanishes or the ratio is \(\tfrac{0}{0},\) the common factors cancel and \(\dfrac{f(n)}{g(n)} = \dfrac{n - 2}{n - 3} = 1 + \dfrac{1}{n - 3}.\) That’s an integer only when \(n - 3 = \pm 1,\) so \(n = 2\) or \(n = 4.\) But \(n = 4\) kills \(g,\) so only \(n = 2\) survives, and the sum is \(2.\) Therefore, the answer is A.
hints: Both cubics have \(n = -1\) as a root; factor each and cancel common factors
The ratio simplifies to \(\dfrac{n - 2}{n - 3} = 1 + \dfrac{1}{n - 3};\) it is an integer only when \(n - 3\) divides \(1\)
